entries.title: Revelation of John 4:1
segments: After these things. Here begins a second vision or group of visions, that of God's presence in Heaven, the background of all that follows.  The main divisions in the Book of Revelation are marked by this phrase.  See

.
 

 
 Come up hither.   John was lifted up in Spirit, as was Ezekiel, to behold the visions of God.   See

segments: I was in the spirit. See

and note thereon.
 

 
 Set in heaven. Already there, not placed there as a part of the vision.
 

 
 One sitting. The Eternal God.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 4:3
segments: Like a jasper stone, etc.  These comparisons are made to suggest the splendor of the great king.

entries.title: Revelation of John 4:4
segments: Elders. Like the elders in the synagogues and in the early assemblies of Christians, these 'older men' are in some way representative of the church.

entries.title: Revelation of John 4:5
segments: Lightnings, etc. Expressive of the majesty of the Most High, creating terror in the hearts of men.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 4:6
segments: Crystal. Emblematic of great splendor.  See

.  Symbolical, it would seem, of all created things.
 

 
 Full of eyes. Symbolizing the power of attention and vision.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 4:7
segments: The first creature, etc.  In Ezekiel there are four composite figures, each having four faces.  Here there are four figures, each with a different aspect.  The lion is the noblest of wild beasts; the ox, the strongest of domesticated animals; and the eagle is the most wonderful of flying creatures; with them stands man, nobler and stronger and more wonderful than all.  The wings, as in Isaiah, show their readiness and power for service.

entries.title: Revelation of John 4:11
segments: Worthy art thou. The adoration is offered by the church and the whole creation, and is based here on the fact that God's will and His work are shown in that which He has made.
